name: jev-session-checks
goal: Prove local Codex sessions automatically review Harness source using cached Jev judgments and honest advisory status, without exposing credentials.

evidence: Defined background advisory startup/resume checks for governed local projects, isolated credential transport, cache reuse, explicit failure status and mandatory Codex trust. Baseline regression: vitest run test/session-hooks.e2e.test.ts exited 1 with 7 failures; unknown session command.

Added the session hook runner and idempotent global installer, restricted to governed roots and associated Git worktrees. Installed owner-only stable bundle and settings using the dedicated Harness credential reference. Normal Codex hook review marked the exact definition trusted and active.

The same 7 CLI regressions changed from baseline exit 1 to 7 passing. Eight focused unit tests also pass, including payload minimization, credential isolation, fail-fast provider errors and worktree scope. No live Jev credential probe was run.

bun run check exited 0: 180 CLI unit tests, 56 CLI E2E tests, 1 packaged-report test and 84 report unit tests passed; 25 opt-in live tests were skipped. Formatting, types, lint, builds and both Harness audits passed. Installed-bundle dry run exited 0 with 378 eligible files. Codex hooks/list reported one enabled trusted SessionStart hook for the canonical checkout and worktree, no warnings or errors.
